final_narrative:
The enrichment analysis is conclusive: five of the eight metabolites map to **Tryptophan metabolism** (KEGG hsa00380, FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment = 625), and four of those five additionally map to the **Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production** pathway (WP4210, FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment = 1175). L-Tryptophan (C00078) is the unambiguous upstream driver of this cluster, with KEGG reaction-graph BFS confirming two forward branches from it: (1) L-Tryptophan → 5-Hydroxy-L-tryptophan → Serotonin → N-Acetylserotonin → Melatonin (path length 4), and (2) L-Tryptophan → Kynurenine → 3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid → Quinolinic acid → NAD⁺ (path length 4). Serotonin (C00780) and 3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) are verified members of both pathways via `query_pathway_membership`, and Quinolinic acid (C03722) is independently confirmed in Tryptophan metabolism and Nicotinate/nicotinamide metabolism. Melatonin (C01598) is additionally confirmed in Reactome's "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" (R-HSA-209931).

Biologically, these data point to a coordinated shift in tryptophan allocation between the kynurenine arm (producing quinolinic acid, a neurotoxic intermediate and NAD⁺ precursor) and the serotonin–melatonin arm. 3-Methyladenine (C00913) is not a member of either Tryptophan metabolism or Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production [retracted: p53 pathway claim not supported by RaMP/KEGG]. O-Phosphoethanolamine (C00346) is associated with Starch and sucrose metabolism, Synthesis of PE, and Metabolism of lipids [retracted: phosphoethanolamine cycle claim not supported by RaMP/KEGG]. 4-Hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid (C01127) is associated with Arginine and proline metabolism, Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives, and Glyoxylate metabolism and glycine degradation [retracted: TCA-cycle claim not supported by RaMP/KEGG]. None of these three metabolites appear in either the Tryptophan metabolism or Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production pathways.

The simultaneous elevation of metabolites along both the kynurenine–quinolinic acid route and the serotonin–melatonin route is consistent with broad, non-selective induction of tryptophan catabolism at the dioxygenase branch point. Limitations: claims about causal treatment effects on pathway flux cannot be verified from static metabolite abundance data or the KEGG reaction graph alone without time-course or flux data. 3-Methyladenine, O-phosphoethanolamine, and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid are not members of the enriched Tryptophan metabolism or Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production pathways, limiting integration of these three metabolites into the core biological narrative.
